defs.def: a set of words expressing a statement, a question or an order, usually containing a subject and a verb. In written English sentences begin with a capital letter and end with a full stop/period (.), a question mark (?) or an exclamation mark/exclamation point (!). 句子

ex.s: This is how everyone learned to read． We would start off with sentences， then paragraphs， and then stories． It seemed an unending journey， but even as a six﹣year﹣old girl I realized that knowing how to read could open many doors． When mom said， "The C﹣A﹣N﹣D﹣Y is hidden on the top shelf，" I knew where the candy was． My progress in reading raised my curiosity， and I wanted to know everything． I often found myself telling my mom to drive more slowly， so that I could read all of the road signs we passed．

ex.s: A topic sentence is a sentence that states or suggests the main idea or topic of a paragraph.
ex.t: 主题句是陈述或暗示一个段落主要观点或主题的句子。

ex.s: Often, a topic sentence comes at the beginning of a paragraph; sometimes, it appears in the middle or at the end.
ex.t: 通常，主题句出现在段落的开头；有时，它出现在中间或结尾。

ex.s: Fruit and herbal teas Their popularity ____________ Unusual flavours ____________ Health benefits ____________ Learning to learn When writing a summary, don't just combine all the topic sentences.
ex.t: 水果茶和花草茶 它们的受欢迎程度 ____________ 独特的风味 ____________ 健康益处 ____________ 学会学习 写摘要时，不要只把所有的主题句拼在一起。

ex.s: When giving advice, it's usual to give your opinion within your first sentence.
